newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan - "exuberance" comment not shot from hip.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan - "exuberance" comment not shot from hip.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Tuesday said his recent use of the phrase "irrational exuberance" in reference to financial markets was an attempt to explain how developments in asset markets figure into monetary policy decisions.
He said the Fed considered ahead of time the possibility that the comment might affect financial markets.
"It was not a shot from hip," Greenspan said of his comment. "We thought long and in detail that any such statement could very have immediate market effects."

"Our judgment, however, was that if we are endeavoring to explain, as I was in that speech, the whole structure of policy-making as the Federal Open Market Committee implements it, then it would be important to make certain that everyone knows what we look at," he said in response to a question following testimony to the Senate Budget Committee.

Greenspan's remark on "irrational exuberance," which was made in a speech he delivered last month, roiled world financial markets as traders interpreted it as a signal the Fed was concerned that stock prices might have risen too far.
The Fed chief said he would have preferred that his remarks had been read in their full context.
Greenspan told the budget panel that his speech named asset prices as one factor -- in addition to fluctuations in the prices of goods and services -- that can destabilize the economy.

"The issue I raised in that speech was to ask a very important question," Greenspan said. "How do we know when asset prices, which fluctuate all over the place for many reasons -- the vast proportion of (which are) sound and reasonable -- when would we know when that is not the case?"
